name: e.p.t.q.

card.summary: A Korean range of cross-linked hyaluronic acid fillers (JETEMA) used by clinicians for contouring, including published reports of clavicle definition and height-augmentation procedures.
card.aka: e.p.t.q. S 300 / S 500 / eve X; JETEMA HA filler
card.note: Clinician-administered medical procedure; published reports on novel uses are mostly case reports.

quick.overview:
e.p.t.q. is a line of cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers made by JETEMA Co., Ltd. in Korea, with versions such as S 300, S 500 and eve X. In the looksmaxxing community it is mentioned in connection with injectable, non-surgical body and face contouring.

The published medical literature reporting its use describes clavicle (collarbone) definition, vertex augmentation, heel-pad injections for added height, and other contouring, mostly as case reports and reviews of clinical experience. A lab study also compared its rheology with other fillers.
quick.how: The filler is injected by a physician, in the reports using imaging guidance, local anesthetic and either needles or cannulas, into the target tissue. In the case reports the HA gel adds volume at a specific site, and the HA is expected to reabsorb gradually over months to a year or more. This article does not give procedural details.
quick.risks: HA fillers in general can cause bruising, swelling, lumps and, rarely, serious vascular complications. The reports on novel areas are small and early, and authors call for larger and longer studies. Use requires a trained clinician.

lead: e.p.t.q. is a range of cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) fillers made by JETEMA Co., Ltd. of Korea, sold in versions such as S 300, S 500 and eve X.[1][2][3]

Hyaluronic acid is the most common type of dermal filler, is biodegradable, and in most products is cross-linked to slow its breakdown.[4] Fillers can be used to add volume or reshape features. Following the product's name in the literature, researchers have reported using it for clavicular definition, vertex augmentation for height and head contour, and heel fat pad injections for height, in each case as a case report or small series.[1][5][6]

These are reports of novel uses by physicians; they do not establish how reliably any result is achieved, and the authors of several call for larger studies. A separate lab study measured the rheology of E.P.T.Q S500 alongside four other commercial fillers.[7]

chain: HA gel placed by a clinician at a chosen site
Added volume at collarbone, vertex or heel pad
Sharper clavicle line or small height gain
angle.text: The gel adds volume at the injected site. Published case reports describe added clavicle definition and height gains of about 1.2 to 1.7 cm from vertex or heel-pad placement.

infobox: S 300, S 500, eve X (with lidocaine variants)
Medical device (filler regulation varies by country)[4]

paras: The products named in the studies include e.p.t.q. Lidocaine S 300, S 500 and eve X, from JETEMA Co., Ltd., Korea.[1][2][3][5] Dermal fillers are regulated as medical devices; in the US a provider must administer them, whereas in the UK and EEA they are non-prescription devices injected by licensed persons.[4]

Clavicular enhancement: a 2026 review in the Journal of Craniofacial Surgery covers subperiosteal HA filler for clavicular contouring using e.p.t.q. S 500, reporting consistent skeletal definition, high patient satisfaction and rapid recovery with minimal downtime.[1]

Height augmentation: a case report of a 37-year-old man with injection into each calcaneal fat pad reported an immediate 1.2 cm gain that persisted as 1.7 cm at six months and one year, with high satisfaction.[5] A report of vertex augmentation in a 42-year-old man described a sustained 1.2 cm height increase with no adverse effects at six months.[6]

Other body areas: published reports also describe penile girth augmentation, where a single case showed circumference rising from 12.3 to 13.0 cm,[2] and vaginal augmentation in 42 women assessed at baseline, 6 and 12 months.[3]

The published work consists mostly of case reports and a review of clinical experience: clavicle (review),[1] heel pad (one patient),[5] vertex (one patient),[6] penile girth (one patient),[2] and vaginal augmentation (42 women).[3] The authors of the case reports say larger studies and longer follow-up are needed. A laboratory study found that the rheological properties of E.P.T.Q S500 and four other high-crosslink fillers did not change after passing through 22-G or 25-G cannulas.[7]

Common effects of dermal fillers include bruising, redness, pain and itching; less common are infection, allergic reactions, scarring and lumps, and rarely blockage of blood vessels causing vision loss.[4] Fillers last roughly six months for many wrinkle products;[4] the reports above describe expected reabsorption of about 9 to 12 months for the product in one use.[3]
The name is associated with hard-looksmaxxing discussion of injectable contouring options; the clinical literature cited here attributes the product to JETEMA.
